assumptions: The transcript is the exons of the named annotation, in the order the location writes them.
Annealing is pydna's, run identically on both templates.
limits: Answers for the ONE transcript named: another isoform of the same gene can behave differently.
A junction-spanning primer is blind to gDNA by construction, not by efficiency — this does not model partial priming.
bio.jane/contract.question: Does this primer pair span an exon junction, and would genomic DNA amplify too?

description: What a primer pair does on a SPLICED transcript versus genomic DNA: the products on each, whether a primer straddles an exon junction (so the assay cannot amplify gDNA at all), whether genomic DNA would still give a band, and by how many bases the two products differ on a gel.

_files.description: The project: record references shaped like _subject. Their records become library documents a tool names in sequences/parts/document; a trace or alignment is found by file name.

_subject.description: The record to act on: exactly one of sequence, accession (+source), sample (an id from list_samples) or file ({name, text} or {name, base64}); record_index picks one record of several.

end_length.description: 3'-most bases that must pair exactly whatever the mismatch budget. Advanced.

limit.description: min 3' footprint match length (pydna `limit`). In bp. Advanced.

mismatches.description: substitutions a primer may carry and still prime (QUEEN `{s<=N}`). 0 is pydna's exact search. Advanced.

transcript.description: the joined mRNA or CDS annotation to splice, by NAME. Left empty the record's only joined annotation is used, and several are refused with their names.

name: analyze_rt_pcr

gdnaWouldAmplify.description: the same pair also makes a product on genomic DNA, so a contaminated RNA prep gives a band

intronBp.description: intron removed by splicing — the size difference between a genomic and a transcript product on the gel

junctionSpanning.description: a primer's own footprint straddles an exon junction, so this pair cannot prime on genomic DNA at all — the property an RT-PCR assay is designed for. Branch a workflow on this

placements.description: per primer: where it binds on the transcript, and which junction offsets its footprint straddles

products.description: one row per product: its transcript interval, its genomic interval, the genomic PIECES a spliced product maps to (several when it spans a junction), and whether it forms on the transcript only, genomic only, or both
